name: Businessmap
description: Businessmap is an enterprise work-management platform for connecting strategic goals, project portfolios, outcomes and team delivery. Organizations use workspaces, boards, workflows and cards to visualize work, coordinate dependencies, govern flow and improve delivery across teams.
agentUseSummary: Businessmap cannot yet be installed in Relay. Its complete API v2 schema is available only inside an authenticated customer account, while the public native MCP setup mounts customer-keyed local stdio packages; Relay requires a reviewed, version-pinned typed wrapper before exposing either surface to agents.

blocked.label: Mount raw Businessmap MCP
blocked.description: Relay does not install or expose the provider's customer-keyed local stdio MCP packages or their introspected tool surface directly to agents.

blocked.label: Install latest packages at runtime
blocked.description: Relay does not execute unpinned `npx @bmapio/mcp-client-*` packages at runtime or permit package updates to change agent authority without review.

blocked.label: Guess account-gated API schemas
blocked.description: Public pages confirm API v2 and selected examples but do not publish the complete current OpenAPI schemas, pagination, error and mutation contracts needed for a typed wrapper.

blocked.label: Expose the full platform surface
blocked.description: Raw workspaces, boards, users, cards, comments, files, analytics, outcomes, administration, automation, bulk operations and exports remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Bypass account roles
blocked.description: Businessmap API v2 inherits the connected user's board roles and action permissions; Relay cannot broaden or substitute them.

blocked.label: Create a second Kanbanize connection
blocked.description: Kanbanize is the former product name and must resolve to this single future Businessmap authority, credential, policy and lifecycle.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Businessmap agent action is enabled until Relay reviews the authenticated OpenAPI contract and implements a version-pinned typed wrapper with explicit bounds, redaction and Safe or Dangerous policy.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw cannot mount raw Businessmap stdio MCP or guessed API v2 calls; a reviewed typed Railway wrapper is required.
Hermes cannot mount raw Businessmap stdio MCP or guessed API v2 calls; a reviewed typed Railway wrapper is required.

providerSetup.blocker: Businessmap publishes an API v2 landing page and selected public examples, but directs customers to the authenticated My Account API tab for the complete official API documentation and interactive OpenAPI surface. Its public native MCP guide instead runs `@bmapio/mcp-client-cards` and `@bmapio/mcp-client-docs` through local `npx` stdio with the customer's subdomain and API key. This worker may not enter the account-only console, capture credentials, mount raw MCP, install latest packages at runtime or invent missing schemas. A typed Relay connector cannot be reviewed for exact paths, fields, pagination, errors, redaction and mutations from the public fragments alone.
providerSetup.nextAction: In the separate provider-console acceptance task, use a disposable tenant and dedicated least-authority API user, open the authenticated API tab, export or record the current official OpenAPI document and exact version, and provide it without secrets to the implementation lane. Then implement a version-pinned Railway adapter with fixed tenant origin, `apikey` header, bounded first-page reads, metadata-only results, allowlisted minimal mutations, collision checks, secret-safe errors, explicit Safe/Dangerous profiles and focused schema-drift tests. Do not mount the raw MCP packages.

evidence.supports: Businessmap confirms its broad API v2 surface and states that the complete official API reference is accessed from the authenticated My Account API tab and tested with an API key.

Businessmap's official MCP guide configures local stdio through `npx @bmapio/mcp-client-cards` and `@bmapio/mcp-client-docs` with customer subdomain/API-key environment variables and introspected tools.
Businessmap recommends dedicated API users, disabling API access for ordinary roles, mapping automation owners and periodically regenerating API keys.
Businessmap states that API v2 actions are controlled by the connected user's board roles and action permissions.
Businessmap identifies Kanbanize as the former product name and confirms continuity for existing software subscribers.
